macro.headline: Bull regime intact but momentum splits: defensives lead, tech drags.
macro.story:
The tape shows a split market. SPY sits at 745.4, up 1.3% over 21 days and still above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, with RSI at 53.5 and MACD holding bullish — a workable but tired uptrend. The Dow is the leader (RSI 59, MACD hist +27), while QQQ and the Nasdaq have gone sideways and slipped below their 50-day, with negative MACD histograms confirming near-term momentum loss. VIX at 16.81 is calm (down 11% over 21d), 10Y yield ticked up to 4.57% (+4.5% in 5d), the 2s10s spread widened sharply (+36% in 5d) toward re-steepening, and DXY firmed to 100.9. Gold and silver remain in downtrends below both major moving averages; WTI is still down 19% over 21 days despite a 5-day bounce.

The tracked conversation frames the causal picture as a tug-of-war rather than a single story. Sentiment leans firmly toward tech-specific caution: the dominant view flags the VXN/VIX ratio spiking to roughly 1.7 — the highest since the dot-com bust — as evidence that tech-sector volatility is decoupling from broad-market calm, with concern clustering around names like DELL, MRVL, AMAT and semi-cap suppliers. That maps directly onto the price data (QQQ below its 50-day, MACD negative, Technology sector rated BEARISH here). At the same time, the tracked conversation also flags easing US financial conditions — described as the loosest since early 2026 and near an 11-year high on that measure — plus Iran-deal de-escalation talk and Micron's $3B US semiconductor capex announcement as offsetting bullish threads. This is a genuine split: sentiment attributes broad-market resilience to loosening financial conditions and geopolitical risk unwind, while attributing tech-specific weakness to elevated single-name volatility and supply-chain names rolling over. The rotation picture in the sector data is consistent with that read — money is moving to Healthcare, Financials, Utilities rather than fleeing risk wholesale.

Sector rotation confirms it: Healthcare (score 9.8, RSI 64) and Financials (9.2, RSI 61) are HOT with bullish MACD, Utilities and Energy are QUALIFYING, and Technology, Real Estate, and Materials are all BEARISH. Only 5 of 11 GICS sectors are above their 50-day. The Early-Runway rotation signal is firing hardest inside Healthcare — Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research, Drug Manufacturers — plus Credit Services in Financials and Staffing in Industrials. This is where the validated tailwind lives right now, not in mega-cap tech.

Forward watch: the bull-regime overlay is intact (SPY -1.9% from 52w high, no defensive flag), so continuation setups in Early-Runway industries remain the primary hunting ground. The washout timing signal is CALM — not engaged. Key risks to monitor: any break of SPY's 50-day near 738, a VIX push back above 20, and whether the QQQ MACD deterioration spreads into the broader tape.
